children.text: An air-tunable Fabry-Perot cavity has inner-surface reflectivity R=0.90 and spacing t=1.00 cm. Its transmission is \(T=[1+F\sin^2(\delta/2)]^{-1}\), \(F=4R/(1-R)^2\), \(\delta=4\pi nt\cos\theta/\lambda\). A sodium lamp, collimator, D1-only filter, etalon and f=30.0 cm imaging lens produce concentric fringes observed by microscope. D1 has λ=589.6 nm. Outer glass faces do not participate in cavity reflections. Use h=\(6.626\times10^{-34}\) J s, e=\(1.6\times10^{-19}\) C, me=\(9.1\times10^{-31}\) kg and c=\(3.0\times10^{8}\) m/s. Vacuum means n=1. Zeeman shifts are mjgkμBB with μB=he/(4πme). Both upper ²P1/2 and lower ²S1/2 levels have J=1/2. Their full splitting gaps are ΔE1<ΔE2. The source diagrams define the four transitions and ring labels.

statement.text:
Fabry-Perot etalon and Zeeman splitting
An air-tunable Fabry-Perot cavity has inner-surface reflectivity R=0.90 and spacing t=1.00 cm. Its transmission is \(T=[1+F\sin^2(\delta/2)]^{-1}\), \(F=4R/(1-R)^2\), \(\delta=4\pi nt\cos\theta/\lambda\). A sodium lamp, collimator, D1-only filter, etalon and f=30.0 cm imaging lens produce concentric fringes observed by microscope. D1 has λ=589.6 nm. Outer glass faces do not participate in cavity reflections. Use h=\(6.626\times10^{-34}\) J s, e=\(1.6\times10^{-19}\) C, me=\(9.1\times10^{-31}\) kg and c=\(3.0\times10^{8}\) m/s. Vacuum means n=1. Zeeman shifts are mjgkμBB with μB=he/(4πme). Both upper ²P1/2 and lower ²S1/2 levels have J=1/2. Their full splitting gaps are ΔE1<ΔE2. The source diagrams define the four transitions and ring labels.

a.i. First three orders
For vacuum find interference orders mi of the first three bright rings counted outwards from the centre.
a.ii. Ring angles
Calculate their incidence angles.
a.iii. Ring diameters
Calculate their image diameters Di.
b.i. Phase linewidth

Find the phase FWHM ε near a transmission maximum.
b.ii. Resolving power
Near normal incidence find λ/Δλ under the criterion that the peak phase separation equals ε.
c. Air refractive index
Slow admission from vacuum to atmospheric pressure produces ten new fringes from the centre. Estimate nair.
d. Four Zeeman frequencies

Write νa,νb,νc,νd. The upper-to-lower mj pairs are a:(−1/2,+1/2), b:(+1/2,+1/2), c:(−1/2,−1/2), d:(+1/2,−1/2).
e. Splittings from ring diameters

For the four rings D1<D2<D3<D4 corresponding to a,b,c,d at the same order, derive ΔE1 and ΔE2 in terms of the measured diameters.
f. Measured Landé factors
At B=0.1 T the diameters are 3.88,4.05,4.35,4.51 mm. Find gk1 and gk2.
g. Solar magnetic field
The shortest-to-longest sodium D1 wavelength separation in a solar region is 0.012 nm. Find B using the Landé factors.
h.i. LED transmitted comb
At normal incidence a vacuum etalon receives an LED band centred at 650 nm with width 20 nm. Estimate the number of transmitted lines.
h.ii. Individual comb linewidth
Find the frequency FWHM of each transmitted line.

children.text: Bright transmission requires 2ntcosθ=mλ. Since 2t/λ=33921.3026, the highest accessible integer is 33921. Thus m1=33921, m2=33920 and m3=33919.
Use \(\theta_i=\arccos(m_i\lambda/(2t))\), obtaining approximately 0.242°, 0.502° and 0.668°. The source rounding gives 0.241°, 0.502° and 0.667°.
\(D_i=2f\tan\theta_i\simeq2f\theta_i\), with angles in radians. The diameters are approximately 2.53, 5.26 and 6.99 mm.
At half maximum Fsin²(ε/4)=1. Thus \(\epsilon=4\arcsin(1/\sqrt F)\simeq4/\sqrt F=0.211\,\mathrm{rad}\).

Each new centre crossing increases optical order by one. Hence \(2t(n_{air}-1)/\lambda\simeq10\), giving \(n_{air}\simeq1+10\lambda/(2t)=1.000295\). The fractional initial order and endpoint counting limit the precision of this estimate.

With ν0=c/λ, \[
u_a=
u_0- rac{\Delta E_1+\Delta E_2}{2h},\quad
u_b=
u_0- rac{\Delta E_2-\Delta E_1}{2h},\] \[
u_c=
u_0+ rac{\Delta E_2-\Delta E_1}{2h},\quad
u_d=
u_0+ rac{\Delta E_1+\Delta E_2}{2h}.\] Each level is displaced by half its full gap.

Paraxial interference gives \(|\Delta\lambda|/\lambda=|D_j^2-D_i^2|/(8f^2)\), and \(|\Delta\nu|=c|\Delta\lambda|/\lambda^2\). Thus \[\Delta E_1=\frac{hc}{8\lambda f^2}(D_2^2-D_1^2)=\frac{hc}{8\lambda f^2}(D_4^2-D_3^2),\] \[\Delta E_2=\frac{hc}{8\lambda f^2}(D_4^2-D_2^2)=\frac{hc}{8\lambda f^2}(D_3^2-D_1^2).\] Experimental rounding makes alternative pairs slightly different.

Divide the E-derived gaps by μBB. Pairs (D2,D1) and (D4,D2) give gk1≈0.68 and gk2≈1.99. Alternative pairs give about 0.72 and 1.95. These are consistent with theoretical 2/3 and 2 within the supplied measurement precision.
The full energy span is (gk1+gk2)μBB≈hcΔλ/λ². Thus \(B=4\pi m_ec\Delta\lambda/[e\lambda^2(g_{k1}+g_{k2})]\). Using the source sum 2.67 gives B≈0.277 T, or 2770 gauss.

The free spectral range is c/(2t)=\(1.5\times10^{10}\) Hz. The LED width is approximately cΔλ/λ²=\(1.42\times10^{13}\) Hz, giving N≈2tΔλ/λ²≈947. The source rounds the bandwidth first and reports 946. Exact endpoint counting depends on the specified band edges.
\(\Delta\nu=c\epsilon/(4\pi nt)\simeq c/(\pi nt\sqrt F)\simeq5.0\times10^8\,\mathrm{Hz}\). This is the individual linewidth, not the 15 GHz free spectral range.

solution.text:
Fabry-Perot etalon and Zeeman splitting
a.i. First three orders
Bright transmission requires 2ntcosθ=mλ. Since 2t/λ=33921.3026, the highest accessible integer is 33921. Thus m1=33921, m2=33920 and m3=33919.
a.ii. Ring angles
Use \(\theta_i=\arccos(m_i\lambda/(2t))\), obtaining approximately 0.242°, 0.502° and 0.668°. The source rounding gives 0.241°, 0.502° and 0.667°.
a.iii. Ring diameters
\(D_i=2f\tan\theta_i\simeq2f\theta_i\), with angles in radians. The diameters are approximately 2.53, 5.26 and 6.99 mm.
b.i. Phase linewidth
At half maximum Fsin²(ε/4)=1. Thus \(\epsilon=4\arcsin(1/\sqrt F)\simeq4/\sqrt F=0.211\,\mathrm{rad}\).
b.ii. Resolving power
\(|\Delta\delta|=4\pi nt|\Delta\lambda|/\lambda^2\). Thus \(\lambda/\Delta\lambda=4\pi nt/(\lambda\epsilon)\simeq\pi nt\sqrt F/\lambda=1.01\times10^6\).
c. Air refractive index
Each new centre crossing increases optical order by one. Hence \(2t(n_{air}-1)/\lambda\simeq10\), giving \(n_{air}\simeq1+10\lambda/(2t)=1.000295\). The fractional initial order and endpoint counting limit the precision of this estimate.
d. Four Zeeman frequencies
With ν0=c/λ, \[\nu_a=\nu_0-\frac{\Delta E_1+\Delta E_2}{2h},\quad\nu_b=\nu_0-\frac{\Delta E_2-\Delta E_1}{2h},\] \[\nu_c=\nu_0+\frac{\Delta E_2-\Delta E_1}{2h},\quad\nu_d=\nu_0+\frac{\Delta E_1+\Delta E_2}{2h}.\] Each level is displaced by half its full gap.
e. Splittings from ring diameters
Paraxial interference gives \(|\Delta\lambda|/\lambda=|D_j^2-D_i^2|/(8f^2)\), and \(|\Delta\nu|=c|\Delta\lambda|/\lambda^2\). Thus \[\Delta E_1=\frac{hc}{8\lambda f^2}(D_2^2-D_1^2)=\frac{hc}{8\lambda f^2}(D_4^2-D_3^2),\] \[\Delta E_2=\frac{hc}{8\lambda f^2}(D_4^2-D_2^2)=\frac{hc}{8\lambda f^2}(D_3^2-D_1^2).\] Experimental rounding makes alternative pairs slightly different.
f. Measured Landé factors
Divide the E-derived gaps by μBB. Pairs (D2,D1) and (D4,D2) give gk1≈0.68 and gk2≈1.99. Alternative pairs give about 0.72 and 1.95. These are consistent with theoretical 2/3 and 2 within the supplied measurement precision.
g. Solar magnetic field
The full energy span is (gk1+gk2)μBB≈hcΔλ/λ². Thus \(B=4\pi m_ec\Delta\lambda/[e\lambda^2(g_{k1}+g_{k2})]\). Using the source sum 2.67 gives B≈0.277 T, or 2770 gauss.
h.i. LED transmitted comb
The free spectral range is c/(2t)=\(1.5\times10^{10}\) Hz. The LED width is approximately cΔλ/λ²=\(1.42\times10^{13}\) Hz, giving N≈2tΔλ/λ²≈947. The source rounds the bandwidth first and reports 946. Exact endpoint counting depends on the specified band edges.
h.ii. Individual comb linewidth
\(\Delta\nu=c\epsilon/(4\pi nt)\simeq c/(\pi nt\sqrt F)\simeq5.0\times10^8\,\mathrm{Hz}\). This is the individual linewidth, not the 15 GHz free spectral range.
